extracted.intended_audience: sellers offering negative-option/subscription features, trade associations, legal counsel, and regulators reviewing FTC compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for sellers to comply with the FTC's Negative Option Rule (consent, disclosure, recordkeeping, and simple cancellation / “click to cancel” requirements for subscription and recurring-charge programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unambiguously affirmative consent to the negative option feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must obtain the consumer's unambiguously affirmative consent to the negative option feature separately from any other portion of the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Rule requires express informed consent to the negative option feature (e.g., a separately presented check box is an example). The Commission offered examples (check box, signature, or substantially similar method) but does not require any single mechanism; the provision applies to the negative option feature only and must enable consumers to demonstrate their agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjacent clear and conspicuous disclosures at time of consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Important information about the negative option feature must be clearly and conspicuously provided immediately adjacent to the request for consumer consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosed information should include that the charge will be recurring, the deadline to act to stop charges, the amount of the charges, and information necessary to cancel. The Commission did not specify exact placement, language, or font size but requires the disclosures be clear and conspicuous and immediately adjacent to the means of recording consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on information or techniques that interfere with consent (anti-dark-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers cannot include any information or employ techniques that interfere with the consumer's ability to understand disclosures and provide unambiguously affirmative consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Rule bars any information that 'interferes with, detracts from, contradicts, or otherwise undermines' the consumer's ability to provide express informed consent. This language captures dark patterns to the extent they undermine consent; the Commission declined to add separate phrasing about dark patterns because the rule already prohibits interfering practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative (not silence) consent required
rubrics_metrics.description: Consent must be affirmative; consumers cannot give consent through silence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under §425.5 consumers must give affirmative consent. The Commission declined to add extra language stating consent cannot be given through silence because the affirmative-consent requirement already addresses it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of verification of consumer consent — three year retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must obtain and maintain verification of each consumer's consent to the negative option feature for a period of three years from the date of consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final Rule modifies the NPRM's longer or conditional retention periods to a three-year-from-consent standard to balance enforcement needs against privacy and small-business burdens. Sellers may destroy records sooner only if they qualify for the technological exemption. Maintaining copies of advertisements or telephone scripts alone does not satisfy this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological exemption to recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers need not retain consumer consent records if they can show by a preponderance of the evidence that their processes make it technologically impossible for a consumer to purchase the good or service without providing unambiguously affirmative consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exemption allows sellers who implement processes that prevent enrollment without affirmative consent to avoid the recordkeeping requirement. The seller bears the burden of demonstrating it meets the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of ads or telephone scripts do not substitute for consumer-specific consent records
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining copies of advertisements or telephone scripts documenting disclosures does not meet the recordkeeping requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such generic materials can be manipulated and cannot show any particular consumer received the disclosures prior to giving consent. Sellers must either maintain records of each consumer's unambiguously affirmative consent or demonstrate they satisfy the technological exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplar consent mechanisms and 'substantially similar' methods allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Check box, signature, or 'substantially similar' method were offered as examples of mechanisms to obtain unambiguously affirmative consent; the Rule does not mandate a specific mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'substantially similar' is intended to cover methods affording the same protections as a check box or signature and to allow for technological advancement without tying sellers to specific mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: No separate consent required for the 'rest of the transaction'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission removed the proposed requirement that sellers obtain separate consent to 'the rest of the transaction' apart from the negative option feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given required disclosures adjacent to consent and other protections, a separate consent to the remainder of the transaction was found unnecessary, confusing, and hard to implement; however, the separate affirmative consent to the negative option feature itself remains required.

rubrics_metrics.name: No additional separate consent required for free-trial conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declines to require separate affirmative consent at the conclusion of a free trial for conversion to a paid negative option feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the seller follows the Rule's disclosure and consent requirements at enrollment, consumers should understand enrollment and impending charges after a free trial. The Commission may consider reminders (e.g., annual reminders) in future rulemaking but did not adopt a separate conversion consent requirement here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple cancellation mechanism — overall performance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must provide a cancellation mechanism that (1) immediately halts recurring charges; (2) is as simple to use as the mechanism the consumer used to consent to the negative option feature; and (3) is readily accessible through the same medium the consumer used to provide that consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a performance-based standard intended to set guardrails while allowing flexibility. The mechanism must be cost-effective, timely, and easy to use and cannot include unreasonable barriers that impede effective cancellation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'as simple as' (symmetry) for cancellation vs. consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'as easy as' standard requires similar cancellation and consent experiences in terms of time, burden, expense, and ease of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable verification, authentication, or confirmation (e.g., identity verification) is permitted, but such procedures should not create unreasonable asymmetry. Any authentication or verification that creates unreasonable asymmetry or is used to thwart or delay cancellation violates section 5 and the Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same-medium requirement is a floor, not a ceiling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rule requires sellers to provide a simple cancellation mechanism through the same medium (internet/interactive electronic medium, telephone, in-person, mail) the consumer used to consent; sellers may also provide additional cancellation methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves consumer ability to cancel in the manner they signed up while allowing sellers to offer other options. The Commission retained authority to require same-medium cancellation given the record of unfair practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online cancellation: easy to find and equivalent online experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a consumer enrolls online (website, mobile app, chat, email, or messaging), sellers must afford an equally simple online cancellation experience that allows consumers to easily find and use the cancellation mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cancellation mechanism need not be the exact same interface used to enroll but cannot be more difficult to use or find. Examples include a clearly-labeled cancellation button in account/user settings or a prominent link. Sellers cannot satisfy the obligation merely by providing location info at enrollment if the mechanism is not easy to find later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'interactive electronic medium'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Interactive electronic medium' is used instead of 'internet' and includes all methods of electronic communication (except telephone calls), including text, chat, email, websites, and mobile apps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This broader definition covers cancellation via chat, text messaging, email, and other electronic means and is meant to align coverage with consumer expectations and technological realities (e.g., MMS vs SMS distinctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for live/virtual agent cancellation mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancellation mechanisms that require interaction with a live or virtual agent are not considered an acceptable online cancellation mechanism unless the consumer originally consented through such a live/virtual agent mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses consumer frustration with having to engage representatives to cancel when enrollment was a quick click; requiring live-agent cancellation is excluded unless it mirrors the mechanism used for consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone cancellation minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: When consent was obtained by telephone, sellers must provide a telephone number and 'assure' calls are answered promptly during normal business hours and are no more costly than the call to enroll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes answering in a comparable timeframe to sign-up calls, permitting automated systems outside business hours if adequate, and prohibiting practices like hanging up on callers attempting to cancel, placing them on unreasonably long hold, providing false information, or misrepresenting delays in processing cancellation requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-person cancellation requirements and practical exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For in-person sales, sellers must provide online or telephone cancellation mechanisms in addition to in-person cancellation where practical; sellers should not require in-person-only cancellation where it creates unfair burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumers raised fairness concerns (pandemic, relocation, mobility issues). Some industries may justify in-person requirements to verify identity or for safety (e.g., alarm services), but such verification must not create unreasonable asymmetry or be used to thwart cancellation.
